source.note: Historical reported cases from the EditedGex iterative checkpoint. Importing them does not re-verify anything: each lesson stays historical-documented, and cited functions are linked only to what their retained artifacts establish today.

lessons.title: Small zero fill of consecutive words matched an inlined memset
lessons.summary: The three-word mantissa clear matched a compiler-inlined memset(..., 0, 12). Three independent stores, a chained assignment and an explicit zero return did not match.
lessons.action: Try memset(pointer, 0, exact byte count) over the stored range instead of separate stores or chained assignments.
lessons.expectedEffect: xor of one register followed by consecutive dword stores through one base register, as in the target.
lessons.limits: Byte count must equal the stored range. The observed function compiled as C with a /G3 per-function contract.
lessons.verification: Strict relocated byte comparison of the whole function.
caveats: No larger object or array semantics are claimed from the stored byte range.
Exact bytes do not establish that the original source used memset.

lessons.title: rep stos over a fixed word count matched memset
lessons.summary: The start-door routine matched memset over exactly 36 words, emitted as xor eax + mov ecx, 36 + rep stosd.
lessons.action: Try memset over the exact byte count (word count x 4) of the destination.
lessons.expectedEffect: xor eax; mov edi, destination; mov ecx, count; rep stosd.
lessons.limits: Observed under the baseline C++ contract. The count and destination come from the pinned bytes, not from a recovered declaration.
lessons.verification: Strict relocated byte comparison of the whole function.
caveats: No object layout is inferred for the destination.
Target-specific code generation; not a portability claim.

lessons.title: A forwarding wrapper passed a stack argument its reference callee signature hides
lessons.summary: SCRIPT_KillPlayer loads and forwards the SECOND stack argument, then returns the first. EditedGex's callee signature hides the unused argument, so copying its one-argument wrapper pseudocode was insufficient.
lessons.action: Read which stack slot is loaded before the call and declare the callee with the forwarded parameter the bytes show, rather than the reference signature.
lessons.expectedEffect: mov eax, [esp+8]; push eax; call; mov eax, [esp+8]; add esp, 4; ret.
lessons.limits: Stack displacements shift after each push; compare the loaded slot, not the literal offset.
lessons.verification: Strict relocated byte comparison, including the call relocation.
caveats: The forwarded argument is an observation from the bytes, not a recovered API declaration.

lessons.title: Pre-incremented argument readers matched under /G3, not /G5
lessons.summary: The argument readers need a pre-incremented four-byte slot followed by a load from the previous slot. /G5 inserted an extra NOP in _get_int_arg; /G3 reproduced the original bytes. The short reader returns AX rather than a value assembled from the undefined upper half of EAX.
lessons.action: Increment the slot pointer first and read the previous slot; if bytes differ only by scheduling padding, a per-function /G3 contract is a candidate experiment that needs explicit approval.
lessons.expectedEffect: No NOP between the increment and the previous-slot load.
lessons.limits: Scoped contract observation for these readers. A flag override is a per-function compiler-contract change and is never applied automatically.
lessons.verification: Strict relocated byte comparison under the approved per-function contract.
caveats: Not permission to change global flags.
Exact bytes under /G3 do not prove the original compiler flags.

lessons.title: Forwarding-only callbacks matched with opaque pointer parameters
lessons.summary: The collision callbacks simply forward two pointers to a callee. An opaque pointer was sufficient; inventing an object layout for these wrappers added no evidence.
lessons.action: Declare the forwarded parameters as opaque pointers (void *) and pass them through unchanged.
lessons.expectedEffect: Two stack loads, two pushes, one call, caller cleanup of 8 bytes.
lessons.limits: Only for code that forwards without dereferencing.
lessons.verification: Strict relocated byte comparison, including the call relocation.
caveats: No GXObject or other object layout was inferred or proven.

lessons.title: Language, flag and reference-parameter variants did not remove a register-allocation mismatch
lessons.summary: For the byte-assembly readers, C mode, /G3 and C++ reference-parameter variants did not remove the ECX/EDX allocation mismatch. For 0041fba0, C and /G3 variants did not improve the comparison at that checkpoint.
lessons.action: Do not retry these variant families without a new hypothesis or a changed compiler/binding basis; look for a structural source difference instead.
lessons.expectedEffect: Identical resolved output when only these variants change.
lessons.limits: Scoped to these functions under the contracts recorded at the time. Not a claim that these variants never work elsewhere.
lessons.verification: Compare resolved output identities across candidates under the same basis.
caveats: 0041fba0 was later proved exact by a different change; the negative result concerns only the variants listed.
A changed basis (compiler, binding or target) makes a retest new information.
